anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 instance is a finite isometric block pile with four unsealed targets, one lava hazard, one support block, discrete view rotation, and click-to-mine actions. Lanternfin at d4 requires closed-loop control of a projected 3D body with four signed control channels and simultaneous position, attitude, speed, and duration constraints. Lanternfin has more continuous control and spatial state, but lacks the voxel task's blockers, hazards, inventory/durability management, and route of dependent mine actions.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 instance controls a 2D momentum ball through three ordered lamps, walls, wells, and a cup, using full analog drag. It has route topology and hazards that Lanternfin d4 does not, while Lanternfin adds a 3D projected target and independent tail, yaw, pitch, and roll channels, plus an arrival attitude and speed gate. The two tasks are different control problems; Lanternfin is credibly above this L3 anchor on control dimensionality and 3D state, but the missing route and hazard structure makes an L4 placement provisional rather than calibration-proven.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 instance requires four adjacent swaps on a changing 5x5 board, at least seven cascade waves, a refill preview, an exact score, and avoidance of licorice. Each accepted swap changes the information and later decision problem, with replayed cascade and refill state. Lanternfin d4 instead presents one visible pearl and a continuous feedback-control problem; its physical trajectory is nontrivial, but it has no branching combinatorial board, multi-round dependency, exact score, or forbidden-cell management. It is below this L5 anchor.

visible_baseline_solution: From screenshots and visible controls, identify the pearl and fish in the projected tank, use the telemetry and successive frames to steer toward the pearl, and apply the tail, yaw, pitch, and roll controls while keeping speed and attitude bounded. Use camera drag only to improve view. Once the fish is within the arrival radius, below the speed limit, and within the upright pitch/roll limits, maintain that state for the required hold duration and click Certify Dive. The full surface uses held key pairs A/D, J/L, I/K, and Q/E; key release returns the corresponding channel to neutral.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The source implements a four-channel 3D closed-loop docking task. At d4 the target is a long diagonal displacement with a substantial initial attitude disturbance; success requires simultaneously managing translation, heading, pitch, roll, speed, uprightness, and a twelve-tick hold. This is materially more than the approved L1 voxel interaction and is more control-dimensional than the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board, while remaining below the approved L5 Candy Cascade's changing-board dependency and exact multi-constraint planning. The d4 label is therefore a defensible source-based placement, but not empirically calibrated.

concise_summary: Keep Lanternfin Dive at d4/full provisionally. Its actual baseline is a four-channel 3D closed-loop docking task with coupled translation and attitude control, narrow speed and orientation bounds, and a twelve-tick stable hold. It sits above the approved L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine and is plausibly above the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board, while remaining below the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade's dependent changing-board planning. The d1 tail-only wording is not enforced by the implementation.
limitations: This audit did not run browser, human, agent, VNC, or runtime checks.
The proposed placement relies on source comparison rather than measured completion time, error rate, or action burden.
D5 has larger displacements and tighter bounds but also larger damping and gains, so the d4-to-d5 ordering needs empirical confirmation.
Historical preservation could not be established without a pre-controls snapshot.
